newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU OKAYS BELGIAN JOBS PLAN, GIVES FRANCE MORE TIME.
newsitem.headline: EU OKAYS BELGIAN JOBS PLAN, GIVES FRANCE MORE TIME.

text.p: The European Commission cleared on Tuesday a Belgian scheme to cut social security charges on manual workers' wages after banning a previous scheme which gave tax breaks to export-led companies only.
But it delayed by a further two weeks its rejection of French measures to help the textile industry, which in many ways are similar to the old Belgian scheme.
The Commission said Belgium's new Maribel plan was acceptable because it involved general measures to preserve blue-collar work rather than sectoral schemes which distort fair competition.

"The proposed regime was considered to be a general measure and not an aid, given its general and automatic aspect and because it does not discriminate between sectors," the Commission said in a statement.

Maribel IV, as it is known, will allow all Belgian companies to save between 20,000 and 33,000 Belgian francs in social security charges per year per worker, depending on the proportion of manual workers in the total workforce.
The Belgian authorities have excluded financial services and the energy sector from Maribel because of the low percentage of manual workers they employ.
Companies with five workers or fewer will be able to reduce contributions by a flat 34,000 Belgian francs a year per worker.

On March 12, the Commission found the French textile scheme, in force since July 1996, unacceptable because it would transfer unemployment problems to other regions in the EU. But it delayed a decision by two weeks to give France time to revise the rules.
On Tuesday it agreed to give France two more weeks, but sources close to European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert said that this would not prevent a negative decision on the current rules.
The French authorities have indicated that they intend to follow the Belgian path and extend the rules to labour-intensive sectors and particularly manual workers.
